title: Effective fpqc descent of quasi-separated etale spaces over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and work in the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:T\to S$ be an fpqc morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $E'$ be an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] with a chartwise etale morphism $E'\to T$ [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism]. Assume this morphism is quasi-separated: its relative diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. Give $E'$ a descent datum $\theta:p_1^*E'\simeq p_2^*E'$ over $T\times_ST$, equal to the identity on the diagonal and satisfying $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$ on $T\times_ST\times_ST$; products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then there are an algebraic space $E$, a chartwise etale morphism $E\to S$, and an isomorphism $E\times_ST\simeq E'$ inducing this datum. Morphisms between two such descended etale spaces correspond bijectively to morphisms between their pullbacks compatible with the data. No quasi-compactness of $E'$ is assumed, and neither $E'$ nor $E$ is required to be separated.

source.place: Agent trait-specific extension of Rydh Theorem (5.17), author version 2010-03-03, p.22, by descent-stable quasi-compact opens; Theorem (5.3), pp.18-19, supplies full faithfulness. The general theorem (5.17) alone assumes a quasi-compact etale object and is NOT the statement here. Closed and generic field fibres and flat-compatible schematic closures supply the additional trait argument; see report.md. Supporting field descent: Stacks descent.tex Tag 0APK.
